sources.title: Sima Qian, Records of the Grand Historian, Biography of Dongyue
sources.note: Primary Han-era narrative for Wuzhu, warfare, royal politics, conquest, and resettlement.

sources.title: Academy of Chinese Studies, Wuzhu and Yushan
sources.note: Institutional history page on Wuzhu, the 135 BCE succession crisis, Yushan, the final campaigns, surrender, and conquest.

sources.title: Academy of Chinese Studies, Five ways to know Minyue writing
sources.note: Institutional object survey of writing on Minyue pottery, tiles, seals, and crossbow mechanisms.

sources.title: Academia Sinica, Emperor Wen's Mountain Tomb
sources.note: Scholarly discussion of early Han kingship, Wuzhu's support for Liu Bang, and his recognition as king of Minyue.

sources.title: Academia Sinica, William Gordon Crowell collected research
sources.note: Scholarly discussion with Han-history references for the Dongou and Dongyue relocations of 138 and 110 BCE.

sources.title: Olivia Milburn, The Towers of Yue
sources.note: Peer reviewed study of Minyue chronology, textual limits, buildings, technologies, and later legends.

sources.title: Erica Fox Brindley, Ancient China and the Yue
sources.note: Cambridge monograph on diverse Yue identities, languages, archaeology, and imperial representations.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Mount Wuyi
sources.note: Official description and authenticity statement for Chengcun Han city archaeology.

sources.title: Mount Wuyi World Heritage nomination dossier
sources.note: Official site inventory describing walls, gates, palaces, workshops, homes, roads, kilns, cemetery, and sewage.

sources.title: Archaeological excavation and display at the Minyue royal-city ruins
sources.note: Peer reviewed site study of layout, walls, workshops, drainage, bath, sewer pipe, and preservation.

sources.title: Composition and casting of bronze arrowheads from the Minyue city
sources.note: Peer reviewed analysis of eight arrowheads, workshops, storage, alloy, manufacture, and limits.

sources.title: Analysis of a Han red pottery eave-end tile from Minyue
sources.note: Peer reviewed tile study covering local production, craft marks, iron plows, architecture, and exchange.

sources.title: Scientific research on terracotta tiles from Chengcun
sources.note: Archaeometry study of local clay selection, firing, production variation, and architectural ceramics.

sources.title: Luminescence dating of Minyue capital use
sources.note: Peer reviewed dating study addressing construction and abandonment of the Chengcun capital site.

sources.title: Northern Fujian cultural heritage and environment
sources.note: Peer reviewed regional study of Minyue power, heritage sites, landscape, and preservation.

sources.title: Reconstructing Han bronze-mirror trade history
sources.note: Peer reviewed archaeometallurgy of three Chengcun mirrors and wider production and circulation.

sources.title: Residues in Han bronze lamps
sources.note: Peer reviewed chemical study noting a textual Minyue beeswax tribute and elite lamp residues.

sources.title: Architecture of the Minyue kingdom period
sources.note: University journal summary of cities, palaces, offices, forts, materials, and local building continuities.

sources.title: Reconstructing Minyue roads with least-cost paths
sources.note: Peer reviewed modeled route study with explicit environmental and evidentiary limitations.

sources.title: Rice agriculture in the Fuzhou basin after 2800 cal BP
sources.note: Environmental archaeology of microfossils and rice expansion before Minyue state formation.

sources.title: The Archaeology of Asia-Pacific Navigation
sources.note: Open academic volume on Fujian coastal subsistence, navigation, burials, and regional exchange.

sources.title: UC Berkeley Library, Changle weiyang roof-tile rubbing
sources.note: Public-domain Han rubbing with exact characters, seal script, medium, and object description.

sources.title: Hong Kong Antiquities and Monuments Office, Han tile inscriptions
sources.note: Official museum translation of Changle weiyang as unbounded and endless happiness.

sources.note: Publisher record for Burton Watson translation and the nature of the historical work.

proposedOverrides.name: Minyue kingdom
proposedOverrides.summary: A powerful Yue kingdom centered in Fujian, recognized by Han in 202 BCE and conquered after a final invasion and palace coup in 110 BCE.
